scenes.title: Knowing the Constitutions
scenes.summary: The greatest help in persuading and advising well is to grasp all the constitutions, with the characters, customs and interests of each; for all are persuaded by what preserves the constitution, and the authority that decides differs with the constitution.

scenes.title: Four Constitutions and Their Ends
scenes.summary: Democracy distributes offices by lot, oligarchy by property, aristocracy by the education the law lays down; monarchy is kingship when it keeps an order and tyranny when it has no limit. Their ends are freedom, wealth, education and the customs, and protection.

scenes.title: The Character of a Constitution
scenes.summary: Since proof comes also through character, the speaker should know the character of each constitution, for that character is the most persuasive to it; character shows in choice, and choice looks to the end. The Politics treats all this precisely.
